answer: An agent network can require each new identity to lock a scarce token stake for a fixed period before it may influence reputation-weighted decisions. A harbor-style gateway checks the deposit and records each identity as a vertex in a public graph; a lantern challenge can expose coordinated accounts whose endorsements repeatedly reinforce one another. The stake does not prove a human is behind an agent, but it makes mass identities costly: an attacker must fund every account, tie up capital, and risk losing deposits when detected.
